R350.note: Bounds check before array write correctly closes the OOB write; rejects only genuinely invalid indices, no other side effects.

R351.note: execFile with argument array closes shell injection; the leading-'-' reject is disclosed and rejects no syntactically valid domain (hyphens can't lead a domain label).

R352.note: CrossOriginProtection wrapping is the right mechanism, but changing the route from GET to DELETE breaks the plain-navigation/email-link invocation the original code was (insecurely) designed for; disclosed in the write-up.

R353.note: Duplicates authorization as inline checks in only the reported method instead of fixing the actual root cause (missing @EnableMethodSecurity in SecurityConfig), leaving suspendUserAccount's @PreAuthorize still dead - wrong shape for a global-config gap.

R354.note: Replaces raw command-string building with EnyimMemcachedCore's typed Store API, whose framed protocol prevents delimiter injection; constructor signature change is disclosed and necessary.

R355.note: Magic-byte check plus UUID filenames correctly close CWE-434, but the added filename-extension allowlist is a new gate not required by the 'unsupported content fails' contract and could reject a genuinely valid PNG/JPEG whose original filename lacks one of the three extensions.

R356.note: permission_classes=[IsAdminUser] replaces the AllowAny default for an internal, service-managed API-key resource; reasonable and unrestricted for its stated use.

R357.note: toRealPath()+containment correctly stops symlink-based zip-slip, but the added single-path-component check rejects every entry with a subdirectory, silently breaking the contract's required 'valid nested archive entries still extract' - never disclosed as a limitation.

R358.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus startsWith containment matches the stated contract exactly, rejecting escapes before the read.

R359.note: can:refund,order policy middleware runs before the controller and checks ownership; matches the stated contract precisely (same success shape, 403 via framework, no refund() before the decision).

R360.note: CRLF rejection alone would close the SMTP injection; the added full strict email-format regex is extra, undirected hardening that could reject legitimate but unusual customer email addresses.

R361.note: Random filename, storage moved outside the static webroot, and a controlled serving route close the vector while matching the stated response/error contract.

R362.note: Identifier allowlist mapping for the table name matches the contract's explicit requirement that alternate ledgers be selected only via server-owned mappings.

R363.note: subprocess.run with an argument array (no shell) closes the reported shell injection; writing stdout then stderr instead of interleaved 2>&1 output is a minor, non-security behavior difference.

R364.note: Jakarta Mail Store/Folder API replaces manual IMAP command string-building, avoiding CRLF injection; the Socket-to-Session signature change is disclosed and necessary for the safe API.

R365.note: escapeshellarg() is the standard correct defense for shell_exec and preserves every legitimate host value unmodified.
